title: Token-path attribution and span-synthesis for composite requests
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds token-path attribution metrics, synthesized composite request spans, new dashboards, and tuned alerts for token-cost regressions and long-tail latency.
description:
Summary: Instrument the serving runtime and tracing pipeline to produce token-path attribution (mapping tokens to logical request phases and upstream inputs) and to synthesize compact 'composite request' spans for multi-turn or multi-tool requests. This reduces trace cardinality for high-throughput workloads while preserving per-token cost and latency attribution for debugging and billing.

Motivation and context: We've seen two recurring pain points in production: (1) exploding trace volume for composite requests (e.g., routing->tooling->model->postprocess) which makes waterfall analysis noisy and expensive, and (2) difficulty attributing token-level latency/cost back to business inputs when a single user request fans out to multiple model calls. This PR implements an instrumentation pattern that attaches a lightweight token-path tag to token metrics and synthesizes a single high-level span summarizing per-phase token counts and costs. This enables: cheaper traces, clear token-cost attribution in dashboards, and targeted alerts when specific phases regress.

Design notes:
- Token-path attribution: every token emitted by the runtime is annotated with a 3-part path: phase (router|model|tool|postproc), model_variant, and route_id. We expose a Prometheus histogram 'redwood_token_latency_seconds' with labels {phase, model, route, bucket} and a counter 'redwood_token_cost_cents' for cost attribution. These labels are sparse and intended for rollup/aggregation rather than per-token retention.
- Span-synthesis: instead of storing every micro-span for each internal hop in high-cardinality traces, the runtime emits a synthesized composite span for the request containing phase summaries (tokens_in_phase, p50/p95 latency per-phase, cost_cents). These composite spans are indexed by trace_id and can be expanded on-demand by linking to a sampling store when deeper inspection required.
- Tradeoffs: we deliberately avoid recording full token contents/inputs in the composite spans for PII reasons; only structural identifiers (route_id, model hash) and numeric summaries are included. This reduces overhead while maintaining observability value.

What changed (high-level):
- runtime/trace/instrumentation: add token path annotation hooks and composite-span builder (serve/runtime/trace_builder.go)
- runtime/metrics: new metrics and Prometheus exposition (serve/metrics/token_metrics.go)
- otel/enrichment: span factory now accepts synthesized summary payloads and optional link to sampled detailed trace (otel/enrich/synth_spans.go)
- dashboards: new observability dashboard JSONs and a Grafana panel bundle for Console (infra/observability/dashboards/token_path_attribution.json)
- alerts: tuned alerts and playbook updates for token-cost drift and per-phase P99 regression (infra/observability/alerts/token_cost_alerts.yaml)
- tests: unit tests for attribution and an integration test that simulates a composite request across router->tool->model and validates metrics and synthesized spans (serve/runtime/trace_test.go, e2e/observability/composite_request_test.go)

Commits (summary):
- 9f1b2c3: Add token-path types and runtime hooks
- 3a7e4d9: Emit token-level metrics with phase labels
- b12c7e1: Implement composite span synthesizer and otel exporter changes
- d8f4aa2: Add dashboards and alert rules
- e3c01b4: Integration test and perf guard rails
- f45a692: Address lint/coverage feedback and optimize allocations

Files changed (representative):
- serve/runtime/trace_builder.go (new)
- serve/runtime/trace_test.go (new)

Testing and CI: Initial CI run had a lint failure (unused var in token_metrics.go) and a flaky e2e timeout. I pushed two followups: fixed the lint issue and increased the e2e harness timeout; subsequent CI passed: unit tests, linters, and the observability integration suite. Performance microbenchmarks (local perf-canary) indicate ~1.4% additional CPU at 2k rps for the instrumentation in default sampling mode; the overhead is configurable and off by default for self-hosted Private installs.

Review conversation (high level timeline):
- Amit Patel (reviewer): "What is the retention/backfill impact for our existing traces? Will synthesized spans break downstream trace rollups?" — Answered: synthesized spans are additive (new span_kind 'composite') and don't alter existing span ids; rollups use the composite span as a lightweight summary and we added a migration to backfill summaries only for traces sampled after the rollout date.
- Lena Rodriguez (reviewer): "Please ensure token_cost_cents is computed using the same pricing table as billing; adding tests to assert parity." — Action: added unit test comparing token_cost_cents aggregation with billing pricing fixture (serve/metrics/token_metrics_test.go).
- Samir Gupta (reviewer): "Concerned about cardinality explosion on route label. Suggest we canonicalize route ids." — Action: implemented route_id canonicalization and a label whitelist in config; included docs and default whitelist in infra/observability/config_defaults.yaml.
- CI note: first pipeline failed (lint); then author pushed f45a692 which fixed linter and addressed slight allocation issue reported by perf-canary.
- Final approvals: Amit and Lena approved after small followups; Samir approved after whitelist tuning. Merge performed via squash.

Operational playbook additions:
- New alert: OBS-TOKEN-COST-DRIFT triggers when daily rolling 24h token_cost_cents for a route/model deviates >15% vs 7d baseline. Playbook linked in docs/obs/playbooks/token_cost_drift.md.
- New dashboard: 'Token Path Attribution' with panels: per-phase token rate, per-model cost breakdown, P99 per-phase latency heatmap, and sample trace link panel (links to sampled detailed traces).

Backward compatibility and rollout plan:
- The feature is behind a config flag 'observability.token_path_attribution.enabled' default true for hosted and dedicated; default false for Private until private-installer bump.
- Rollout: staged to canary cluster for 48h, then 25% traffic for one week, then global. We added a kill-switch endpoint for immediate disable.

Notes and follow-ups:
- ENG-5821: follow-up to add cost attribution to tenant billing export; will do in a follow-up PR.
- ENG-5902: dashboard perf tuning to pre-aggregate heavy queries into rollup tables.

Merge: merged via squash on 2025-11-07. CI green at time of merge. Change has been documented in docs/obs and added to the Console dashboard bundle for the next release.

Checked boxes: [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] docs [x] perf guard rails [x] alerting/playbook

If you want to try locally: run e2e/observability/run_composite_test.sh which spins up a minimal runtime with token_path_attribution enabled and verifies metrics exported to the local Prometheus instance.

Contact: Maya Chen (author) or Amit Patel for follow-up; see docs/obs/token-path-attribution.md for operational details.
